summary: The Enyaq is Skoda's mid-size electric SUV and the larger sibling to the Elroq, sold in Australia as a conventional SUV and a fastback Coupe across Select 60, Sportline 85 and dual-motor RS grades, all on the MY27 spec. Australian reviewers rate it highly for packaging, real-world efficiency and a cabin that keeps physical controls (CarsGuide 8.3/10, CarExpert 'Very Good'), but they consistently criticise a firm ride and road noise unless the optional adaptive dampers are fitted. The critical buying decision is the price ladder: everything up to the Coupe Sportline 85 sits under the $75,000 FBT cap for novated leasing, while both RS grades sit just above it.
pros: Sportline 85 lists at $60,990 for 551km WLTP and 210kW, undercutting a Tesla Model Y Premium Long Range AWD ($68,900) and a Kia EV5 GT-Line AWD ($71,770) on range per dollar
Genuinely efficient in Australian conditions: CarsGuide averaged 16.6kWh/100km over 970km in the 85 Sportline and saw 13kWh/100km in city running, against a 16.2kWh/100km WLTP claim
585L boot expanding to 1710L in the SUV with Skoda's Simply Clever storage, plus rear-seat head and knee room CarExpert rates strongly in both body styles

MY27 towing is unusually strong for an EV: 2000kg braked on the Sportline 85 grades and 2200kg on the RS (Skoda spec sheet), matching a Zeekr 7X and beating a Tesla Model Y's 1588kg; the Select 60 stays at 1000kg
7-year/unlimited-km warranty plus an 8-year/160,000km battery warranty, with 24-month/30,000km service intervals and pre-paid service packs of $1450 for six years or $1990 for ten
cons: Both RS grades ($76,590 SUV, $77,590 Coupe) sit above the $75,000 FBT exemption cap, so a novated lease loses the exemption that the $66,990 Coupe Sportline 85 still qualifies for

Ride is tuned too firmly without the cost-optional adaptive dampers - CarExpert calls the standard suspension 'much too firm' for Australian roads, and CarsGuide reports tyre roar on coarse-chip surfaces even on 20-inch wheels

The MY27 RS now shares the Sportline's 77kWh usable pack and 165kW DC charging, so its extra $15,600 buys power (250kW, 5.4s to 100km/h) and towing rather than range: 546km WLTP against the Sportline 85's 551km
No spare tyre at any grade, only a repair kit, and the surround-view camera plus semi-autonomous park assist are options rather than standard on Sportline
Safety rating leans on a 2021 five-star Euro NCAP result for the pre-facelift car with no fresh ANCAP assessment, and Skoda now advertises only drive-away offers expiring 31 December 2026
